title: Artifact Restorer in the Palace Museum
synopsis: Master Wang has the arduous but rewarding job of restoring ancient clocks in Beijing’s Palace Museum.

fullText.simplified:
中国人的生活——故宫文物修复师

    早上八点，王师傅准时到达位于故宫内的办公室，准备开始一天的工作。作为故宫文物修复师，王师傅的工作是严谨充实的，但也极其考验耐力。
    王师傅负责宫廷钟表的修复，他的工作是让这些破损的老物件重新焕发光彩。与普通钟表的修复不同，故宫钟表的修复除了要让钟表运转起来，还要遵循“修旧如旧”的文物修复要求，即修复后的钟表要回归到文物本身的状态。因此修复过程非常复杂，用时也特别长。一个钟表的修复工作一般为期几个月，有时一年也很常见。
    整个修复工作分为记录照相、除尘、拆解、清洗、修补、组装调试和整体组装七个环节。每一个环节都要一丝不苟，因为每一件文物都是独一无二的，没有替换的零件。拿到一件需要修复的钟表，修复师首先要记录照相，拍下原始情况，然后细心除尘，再拆解。在拆解环节，修复师可以通过拆解掌握钟表的设计理念和基本结构，初步了解文物。到了清洗环节，修复师需要观察每一个零件，确认是否有缺损并采取相应的修补措施。组装和调试环节则是通过反复调试恢复它的部分机能，这非常需要耐心，因为一个齿轮的摆错都会导致重头再来。最后是整体组装，一步步地从底层、中层到上层，直到完成总体组装咬合。
    由于这样的工作性质，文物修复师必须极具耐心和信念感。故宫采取了传统的师徒制，师父带领徒弟，慢慢地培养。王师傅自己就是16岁那年被师父选中后进入钟表馆的。王师傅入职的第一年，每天都是拧铜丝，或者拆现代闹钟。记忆中，师父总喜欢同时给他两个不同的闹钟。开始他总是小心翼翼地把拆下来的零件分开摆放，师父就会马上把零件混起来。为了把两个闹钟修好，王师傅可谓吃尽了苦头，但也训练出了扎实的基本功。终于到了第四年，王师傅开始修复真正的文物了。现在，故宫钟表馆里过半的钟表都是王师傅修复的。时光荏苒，王师傅已经在故宫工作四十多年了。
    时光染白了少年乌黑的头发，但没有抹去少年的热忱。王师傅快要退休了，他希望退休后能被返聘。他对赚钱没什么兴趣，只是想在工作中延续这份热忱。故宫城墙外的世界日新月异，但城墙内的岁月似乎还是百年前的旧时光。他们是文物修复师，也是时间修复师。
fullText.traditional:
中國人的生活——故宮文物修復師

    早上八點，王師傅準時到達位於故宮內的辦公室，準備開始一天的工作。作為故宮文物修復師，王師傅的工作是嚴謹充實的，但也極其考驗耐力。
    王師傅負責宮廷鐘錶的修復，他的工作是讓這些破損的老物件重新煥發光彩。與普通鐘錶的修復不同，故宮鐘錶的修復除了要讓鐘錶運轉起來，還要遵循“修舊如舊”的文物修復要求，即修復後的鐘錶要回歸到文物本身的狀態。因此修復過程非常複雜，用時也特別長。一個鐘錶的修復工作一般為期幾個月，有時一年也很常見。
    整個修復工作分為記錄照相、除塵、拆解、清洗、修補、組裝調試和整體組裝七個環節。每一個環節都要一絲不苟，因為每一件文物都是獨一無二的，沒有替換的零件。拿到一件需要修復的鐘錶，修復師首先要記錄照相，拍下原始情況，然後細心除塵，再拆解。在拆解環節，修復師可以通過拆解掌握鐘錶的設計理念和基本結構，初步了解文物。到了清洗環節，修復師需要觀察每一個零件，確認是否有缺損並採取相應的修補措施。組裝和調試環節則是通過反覆調試恢復它的部分機能，這非常需要耐心，因為一個齒輪的擺錯都會導致重頭再來。最後是整體組裝，一步步地從底層、中層到上層，直到完成總體組裝咬合。
    由於這樣的工作性質，文物修復師必須極具耐心和信念感。故宮採取了傳統的師徒制，師父帶領徒弟，慢慢地培養。王師傅自己就是16歲那年被師父選中後進入鐘錶館的。王師傅入職的第一年，每天都是擰銅絲，或者拆現代鬧鐘。記憶中，師父總喜歡同時給他兩個不同的鬧鐘。開始他總是小心翼翼地把拆下來的零件分開擺放，師父就會馬上把零件混起來。為了把兩個鬧鐘修好，王師傅可謂吃盡了苦頭，但也訓練出了扎實的基本功。終於到了第四年，王師傅開始修復真正的文物了。現在，故宮鐘錶館裡過半的鐘錶都是王師傅修復的。時光荏苒，王師傅已經在故宮工作四十多年了。
    時光染白了少年烏黑的頭髮，但沒有抹去少年的熱忱。王師傅快要退休了，他希望退休後能被返聘。他對賺錢沒什麼興趣，只是想在工作中延續這份熱忱。故宮城牆外的世界日新月異，但城牆內的歲月似乎還是百年前的舊時光。他們是文物修復師，也是時間修復師。

sentences.simplified: 时光荏苒，王师傅已经在故宫工作四十多年了。
sentences.traditional: 時光荏苒，王師傅已經在故宮工作四十多年了。
sentences.pinyin: shí guāng rěn rǎn wáng shī fu yǐ jīng zài gù gōng gōng zuò sì shí duō nián le
sentences.english: Now, more than half of the clocks in the Palace Museum clock gallery are restored by Master Wang.
Time quickly passes by, and Master Wang has now been working in the Palace Museum for more than 40 years.

sentences.simplified: 时光染白了少年乌黑的头发，但没有抹去少年的热忱。
sentences.traditional: 時光染白了少年烏黑的頭髮，但沒有抹去少年的熱忱。
sentences.pinyin: shí guāng rǎn bái le shào nián wū hēi de tóu fa dàn méi yǒu mǒ qù shào nián de rè chén

sentences.simplified: 王师傅快要退休了，他希望退休后能被返聘。
sentences.traditional: 王師傅快要退休了，他希望退休後能被返聘。
sentences.pinyin: wáng shī fu kuài yào tuì xiū le tā xī wàng tuì xiū hòu néng bèi fǎn pìn
sentences.english: Time has turned the jet-black hair of his youth white, but it has not erased the enthusiasm of his youth.

sentences.simplified: 他对赚钱没什么兴趣，只是想在工作中延续这份热忱。
sentences.traditional: 他對賺錢沒什麼興趣，只是想在工作中延續這份熱忱。
sentences.pinyin: tā duì zhuàn qián méi shén me xìng qù zhǐ shì xiǎng zài gōng zuò zhōng yán xù zhè fèn rè chén
sentences.english: Master Wang is about to retire, and he hopes to be rehired after retirement.

sentences.simplified: 故宫城墙外的世界日新月异，
sentences.traditional: 故宮城牆外的世界日新月異，
sentences.pinyin: gù gōng chéng qiáng wài de shì jiè rì xīn yuè yì
sentences.english: He has little interest in making money but just wants to continue this passion for his work.

sentences.simplified: 但城墙内的岁月似乎还是百年前的旧时光。
sentences.traditional: 但城牆內的歲月似乎還是百年前的舊時光。
sentences.pinyin: dàn chéng qiáng nèi de suì yuè sì hū hái shì bǎi nián qián de jiù shí guāng
sentences.english: The world outside the Palace Museum walls changes with each passing day, ..

sentences.simplified: 他们是文物修复师，也是时间修复师。
sentences.traditional: 他們是文物修復師，也是時間修復師。
sentences.pinyin: tā men shì wén wù xiū fù shī yě shì shí jiān xiū fù shī
sentences.english: .. but the lives of the people within the walls seem to still be in the old times of a hundred years ago.

sentence_translations: Chinese Lives: Artifact Restorer in the Palace Museum
At 8 a.m., Master Wang arrives at his office located inside the Palace Museum, ready to start the day.
As an artifact restorer in the Palace Museum, Master Wang’s job is rigorous and fulfilling, yet also an extreme test of endurance.
Master Wang is responsible for the restoration of the palace clocks.
His job is to make these old, broken objects look good again.
Unlike the common clock repairs, restoration of the clocks in the Palace Museum requires not only making the clocks work, ..
.. but also following the requirement for artifact restoration of “restoring the old as the old”, ..
.. that is, the clocks must be restored to their original state.
Therefore, the restoration process is very complex and time-consuming.
Generally, the restoration of a clock takes several months, and sometimes a year is also common.
The entire restoration process consists of ..
.. seven steps: documenting and photographing, dusting, disassembling, cleaning, repairing, assembling and fine-tuning, and final assembly.
Each step requires meticulous attention because each artifact is unique, and there are no replacement parts.
When given a clock to restore, the restorer first documents and photographs it in its original state, ..
.. then carefully removes the dust before disassembly.
During the disassembly stage, the restorer can grasp the design concept and basic structure of the clock, ..
.. gaining a preliminary understanding of the artifact.
During the cleaning stage, the restorer must observe every part, identify any defects, and take appropriate repair measures.
The assembly and fine-tuning stage involves restoring its partial functionality through repeated fine-tuning.
This requires a lot of patience because one misaligned wheel will cause the whole process to start over.
Finally, there is the final assembly, step by step, from the bottom to the middle, to the top, until everything fits together.
Due to the nature of such work, the restorer must have a great deal of patience and a sense of conviction.
The Palace Museum employs the traditional master-apprentice system, ..
.. with masters guiding apprentices and nurturing their development over time.
Master Wang himself was 16 years old when he was selected by his master and entered the clock gallery.
In his first year on the job, Master Wang spent every day twisting copper wire or dismantling modern alarm clocks.
He remembered that his master liked to give him two different alarm clocks at the same time.
At first, he carefully arranged the disassembled parts separately, but his master would immediately mix them up.
In order to repair both alarm clocks, it could be said that Master Wang suffered a great deal, ..
.. but this also helped train his solid mastery of basic skills.
Finally, in the fourth year, Master Wang began to restore real artifacts.
Now, more than half of the clocks in the Palace Museum clock gallery are restored by Master Wang.
Time quickly passes by, and Master Wang has now been working in the Palace Museum for more than 40 years.
Time has turned the jet-black hair of his youth white, but it has not erased the enthusiasm of his youth.
Master Wang is about to retire, and he hopes to be rehired after retirement.
He has little interest in making money but just wants to continue this passion for his work.
The world outside the Palace Museum walls changes with each passing day, ..
.. but the lives of the people within the walls seem to still be in the old times of a hundred years ago.
They are the restorers of artifacts but also the restorers of time.
